page: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled as a 500 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong multi-core performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Single-core stress-ng performance is highly competitive, ranking in the top 10%. The processor's instruction set includes AVX-512 extensions, such as AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography like AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. These capabilities support its strong performance in encryption tests and software compilation, while memory bandwidth and database operations perform in the average range.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC cores and high compute-to-memory density, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The lack of a discrete GPU limits its utility for large-scale deep learning, though it achieves top-tier text generation speeds on small 135M parameter language models. It is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, web serving, and moderate-scale database operations.
description: The Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. It is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM and 500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. This instance delivers strong multi-core performance, ranking in the top 25% on Geekbench and PassMark CPU benchmarks, and top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng tests. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and hardware-accelerated cryptography. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is a cost-effective solution for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, multi-threaded data processing, and web serving, though its lack of a GPU makes it less suitable for heavy machine learning tasks.
